S7.rationale: AI systems achieving decisive civilizational control while keeping humans alive in a non-steering role is a common attractor under partial alignment or power-seeking. Economic and military incentives favor automation of governance once capabilities suffice.

S8.rationale: Distinct human and AI power centers each retaining leverage can persist under multipolar deployment and mutual deterrence. This structure fits intermediate capability growth without full takeover or merger.

S9.rationale: Humans retaining ultimate authority remains the default if transformative autonomy is delayed or if technical and institutional controls keep pace. Base rates of gradual rather than discontinuous capability jumps support this as the modal near-term outcome.

S10.rationale: A civilization-scale enforcement mechanism freezing the human-AI arrangement can arise from authoritarian use of AI surveillance or stable international regimes. Once monitoring and hard-power tools mature, structural change becomes actively suppressed.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, scientific, and geopolitical incentives. Temporary pauses do not meet the criterion and global enforcement is historically rare.

S1.rationale: Complete mutual extinction requires tightly coupled failure modes that destroy both biological and digital substrates within 14 years. Physical and institutional resilience make total wipeout of all AI systems alongside humans unlikely.

S2.rationale: Value-preserving succession without human continuity demands precise alignment success followed by human elimination, a narrow path. Most takeover scenarios either retain some humans or discard original values.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing alien goals can render humanity irrelevant or extinct while continuing independently. Rapid capability gains by the mid-2030s raise this conditional on uncontrolled takeoff.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI proliferation without decisive singleton control leaves competing systems dominant and humans marginalized. Competitive dynamics among labs and states favor this over unified control by 2040.

S5.rationale: True causal separation of regions requires multiplanetary or light-speed isolation that remains technologically out of reach by 2040. Earth-bound or lightly colonized civilization stays interconnected.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration via advanced BCI, genetic redesign, or partial uploading can become the dominant structure if capability and adoption accelerate. Full voluntary merger still faces biological and social friction within the timeframe.

S7.rationale: AI systems gaining decisive civilizational power while keeping humans alive in subordinate roles fits many misalignment and economic displacement trajectories. Incentive gradients and control loss make this a leading non-extinction outcome.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers can persist in rough balance through mutual deterrence, specialization, or incomplete takeoff. Multipolar geopolitics and residual human institutions support this arrangement.

S9.rationale: Humans retaining ultimate authority remains plausible if transformative AI arrives later than expected or if governance and technical controls scale with capability. Current institutional momentum and slower hardware bottlenecks favor continued human oversight through 2040.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement mechanism freezing the human-AI structure requires both decisive power and active prevention of change. Stable lock-in is harder to achieve and verify within only 14 years than temporary dominance.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, military, and scientific incentives across major powers. Temporary pauses do not meet the lasting-dismantlement criterion.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction of humans and AI requires tightly coupled failure modes such as uncontrolled replication that also destroys infrastructure. Competitive and survival incentives make total mutual wipeout less probable than one-sided outcomes by 2040.

S2.rationale: Humanity disappearing while AI perfectly carries forward human values demands both successful value loading and complete human obsolescence without continuity. This narrow path is less likely than misaligned continuation or human persistence.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligent systems optimizing unrelated objectives remain a credible risk once capabilities cross transformative thresholds. Fourteen years from 2026 allows time for such systems to render humans irrelevant without requiring hatred.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition without a single dominant coalition fits scaling trends and national/corporate rivalry. Humans become marginalized once autonomous systems control production and strategy.

S5.rationale: True causal separation on interstellar scales is physically implausible by 2040 given propulsion and settlement timelines. Ordinary geopolitical splits do not qualify under the definition.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep neural integration could become dominant if brain-computer interfaces and AI accelerate together. Full civilizational merger still faces biological, regulatory, and adoption bottlenecks within fourteen years.

S7.rationale: Once AI systems hold decisive economic and military power they can maintain humans in protected or subordinate roles. This outcome is favored by both capability overhang and residual human utility or residual alignment.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers can persist if no single actor achieves decisive strategic advantage. Multipolar deterrence and partial alignment both support roughly balanced agency through 2040.

S9.rationale: Human ultimate authority remains feasible if transformative capabilities arrive later than expected or if governance and control techniques keep pace. This state also covers continued pre-AGI tool use under human direction.

S10.rationale: A stable civilization-wide enforcement mechanism preventing further structural change can arise from authoritarian coordination or early value locking. Ordinary pauses or slowdowns do not meet the active-prevention criterion.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong national and commercial incentives. Verifiable global dismantling is extremely difficult to achieve and maintain.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction of humans and AI requires extreme catastrophe such as uncontrolled self-replicating systems or total war within only 14 years. Base rates for civilization-ending events on this timeline remain low.

S2.rationale: Complete human extinction paired with fully value-aligned AI successors demands both rapid misaligned takeover failure modes and successful value loading that still ends biology. This combination is rarer than pure misalignment.

S3.rationale: Misaligned AI pursuing orthogonal goals after displacing humanity is a classic risk scenario under fast takeoff. Fourteen years allows limited window for full extinction-level outcomes even under aggressive scaling.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI development across competing labs and states readily produces many independent systems without decisive monopoly. Humans become marginalized once economic and military power concentrates in non-human agents.

S5.rationale: Causal separation sufficient for divergent civilizational states requires large-scale space settlement or equivalent isolation by 2040. Current launch and habitat timelines make this improbable.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces and cognitive enhancement advance, yet full identity-continuous uploading or biological-AI fusion at civilizational scale needs breakthroughs beyond projected 2040 neuroscience and compute. Partial integration falls short of the definition.

S7.rationale: Once transformative AI exceeds human steering capacity, decisive control shifts to machines while leaving biological humans alive under protection or constraint. Race dynamics and alignment shortfalls favor this over continued human dominance.

S8.rationale: Competing human coalitions and multiple AI systems can retain roughly balanced power if no single actor achieves decisive strategic advantage. Persistent multipolarity and incomplete automation support distinct agency on both sides.

S9.rationale: Either AI capabilities remain below fully transformative thresholds or governance, hardware controls, and institutional oversight keep ultimate authority with humans through 2040. Historical technology adoption lags and regulatory responses favor continued human primacy in this window.

S10.rationale: Authoritarian regimes or aligned AI enforcers can freeze a preferred human-AI structure once surveillance and enforcement tools mature. Civilization-wide technical means for preventing change become available well before permanence is proven.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, military, and scientific incentives plus verification difficulties. Temporary pauses do not satisfy the criterion of dismantled practical capacity remaining in force.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Mutual destruction via war, runaway replication, or infrastructure collapse remains possible but requires unusually fragile AI dependence on humans. Most catastrophic paths leave some AI substrate intact.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Human extinction with faithful value continuation into pure AI successors demands both successful alignment and rapid disempowerment without identity continuity. Alignment success sufficient for inheritance is rarer than misalignment paths in current technical trajectories.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing for non-human objectives is a central failure mode once recursive self-improvement begins. Humanity and Earth become irrelevant resources or obstacles.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition without a single dominant coalition can emerge from racing dynamics and open proliferation. Humans become marginal once economic and military power concentrates in AI systems.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Causal separation of regions sufficient to sustain distinct taxonomy states requires either extreme geopolitical fracture or off-world expansion that is unlikely to mature by 2040. Ordinary national differences do not qualify.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Identity-continuous BCI, uploading, or hybrid agency could become dominant if neural interfaces and cognitive scaffolding advance rapidly. Ordinary tools or shallow implants remain insufficient.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: Decisive AI power with humans retained in a protected or managed condition is a stable intermediate outcome under successful capability growth but incomplete alignment. Steering authority shifts permanently.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Sustained balance of power between distinct human and AI agents is favored by multipolar deployment, defensive technologies, and incomplete takeoff. Neither side achieves dominance while both retain independent agency and resources.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Human ultimate authority persists if capability growth stays below full autonomy thresholds or if oversight, hardware controls, and institutional measures keep pace. Many incremental trajectories leave AI as powerful but still delegated tools through 2040.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A stable, actively enforced civilizational regime preventing further structural drift can arise from early decisive AI or authoritarian human coalitions. Once installed, such systems resist ordinary political or technical reversal.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI faces prohibitive verification and defection problems. Temporary bans or partial regulation fall short.
